newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEHMAN WINS GRAND SLAM TOURNAMENT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEHMAN WINS GRAND SLAM TOURNAMENT.

text.p: British Open champion Tom Lehman birdied his first and last holes for a two-under-par 34 over Thursday's last nine holes to win the $400,000 top prize at the Grand Slam of Golf by two strokes over Steve Jones.

Lehman did the best job of adjusting to conditions at the 6,957-yard Poipu Bay Resort course where sunshine and calm air replaced the wet and windy test that confronted the elite foursome through 27 holes on Wednesday.

"I thought it was hard to make putts today," said Lehman, the PGA Tour's leading money winner this year with over $1.7 million. "It seemed as though the greens were grainier this morning and it was difficult to get the speed down."
Lehman, who three weeks ago won the Tour Championship and its $540,000 prize, birdied the 10th and 18th to complete a final-round 66 for a 36-hole total of 10-under 134.
U.S. Open champion Jones closed with a 35 for 136.

Masters champion Nick Faldo of Britain finished third at five-under 139 after a final-nine of two-over-par 38. U.S. PGA champion Mark Brooks also struggled in with 38 to finish a distant fourth at 147.
Only three birdies were made on Thursday. In contrast, the foursome combined for 35 birdies on Wednesday.
"When you start early you don't feel warmed up," said Jones. "For me, I just couldn't get warmed up."
Jones two-putted from 130 feet for par on the 501-yard, par-4 16th and made the day's only birdie besides Lehman at the last hole when his 50-foot eagle chip slid just by.
The nine-hole finish was brought about when heavy rains pounded the island of Kauai on Tuesday, forcing postponement of the first round.
Twenty seven holes were squeezed in on the soggy layout on Wednesday. Players were allowed to lift, clean and place their ball in the fairway both days.

Lehman, who will play in the World Cup and Sun City Challenge in South Africa before closing out his season at the Diner's Club Matches, took a one-stroke lead over Faldo and Jones into the final nine holes.
His opening birdie at the 10th put him two ahead of Jones and three over Faldo, who bogeyed after missing the green left and sliding a six-foot par putt over the right lip.
Faldo, winner of three Masters and three British Opens, bogeyed again at the par-4, 501-yard 16th three-putting from 135 feet and missing an eight-footer for par.
Jones kept pace with Lehman over the final eight holes, but never could make a charge as Lehman played a simple game of fairways, greens and pars.

"It was nice having a two-shot lead at the last hole," Lehman said. "When I hit the green (a 3-iron from 240 yards on the 550-yard, par-5), I felt comfortable. Still, though, I knew it was possible for Steve to chip in for eagle and for me to three-putt."
That didn't happen as Lehman's eagle putt from 35 feet settled within two feet of the hole and the tournament was his.

"When you play with Tom, it's incredible," said Jones, who outdueled Lehman at this year's Open at Oakland Hills. "He's so consistent. He doesn't make many mistakes. By far, I think he's the best player in the world this year."
